review: The hymn is the holiness that gives life: 1:1–8 is Isa 6:3 with Rom 14:11 (every knee) and Ps 147:9 (He feeds the birds), 2:1–8 is Eph 2:4–5 with 1 Cor 6:20 and John 4:14.
Both stanzas are eight lines and the eighth of the second repeats the first line of the first, forming the hymn's inclusio; the payload reproduces the repetition verbatim.

1:8 כָּכָה יָרוּץ עָשְׁרְךָ בְּדָמָהּ — the Arabic هٰكَذَا يَسْرِي غِنَاكَ فِي دِمَاه is 'thus Your riches flow in its blood'; the Hebrew keeps דָּם in the singular and the verb רוּץ, so the line is the Creator's wealth running through a creature's life and not a metaphor of influence.

2:1–2 repeat 'love' twice at the head of the couplet (בְּאַהֲבָה … וּבְעֶצֶם הָאַהֲבָה), following the print's double الْحُبِّ, because the stanza's argument is that love is both the motive and the substance of creation.
